hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? have you ever had a moment so good you wished you could save it?
options: then you’ll love where this light went. listen.
then you’ve seen a little of it. listen.
then this story might help you look. listen.

steps.line: In the Torah’s six days: light, then sky, then land and plants. Then sun, moon and stars. Then fish and birds. Then animals, and people.
Again and again, the story says, “And God saw that it was good.” At the end of the sixth day: “Behold, it was very good.”

steps.q: One of the six days never gets “and God saw that it was good.” Which, and why do the rabbis say so?
o: Day two: dividing isn’t yet good
Day six: people can do harm
Day one: light needed no praise
steps.why: Day two has no “good.” Rashi says the waters weren’t finished until day three, which gets “good” twice. A midrash says it was a day of division, and division isn’t good.

steps.q: The first three days make spaces. The next three fill them. Match each.
steps.why: Rooms, then furniture. Some readers see this pattern in the order of the days.

steps.line: But the rabbis noticed a puzzle. Light on day one, but no sun until day four. So what was that first light?

steps.q: The Talmud has an answer about that first light. What do you think it says?
o: It was the sun, made early
It was a light Adam saw the world by
It was the glow of the angels
steps.why: Chagigah 12a: by that light, the first human could see from one end of the world to the other.

steps.line: The Talmud says it was a special light. By it, the first human could see from one end of the world to the other.
steps.label: a teaching of the rabbis

steps.line: But God saw that later generations would do great harm. So God hid the light away, saved for the righteous in the time to come.
steps.label: a teaching of the rabbis

steps.q: For hiding the light, the Talmud quotes a psalm: “Light is ___ for the righteous.” Which word?
steps.why: Psalm 97:11: “Light is sown for the righteous.” Hidden like a seed, not locked away: it’s meant to come up.

steps.line: Today, some Jewish teachers say a glimpse of that hidden light can still be found: in study, in kindness, in a moment that is simply good.
steps.label: today

say: here’s what i love. the torah never even names the sun and moon here. it calls them the greater light and the lesser light, lamps set in the sky. the first light came before them.
and “good” comes back again and again, like a refrain. the world in this story isn’t an accident or a mess. it’s good, and at the end, very good.

steps.q: By the first light, a person could see “from one end of the world to the other.” What kind of light does that sound like?
o: Light to see things as they are
steps.why: Not only bright. A light for seeing the whole world as it really is. Hasidic teachers say a glimpse of it is hidden in the Torah.

today.say: tonight, learn one line of torah, alone or with someone. a line from this week’s portion is perfect. a hasidic teaching says the hidden light was tucked inside the torah. then name one thing from today that was good.
options: then you’ve gone looking for the hidden light.
and it was good. that’s where the looking starts.

card.keepWhy: Kept, not lost. Look for the good.
sources: Genesis 1:6–31 (the six days; ‘God saw that it was good’; 1:16 the greater light and the lesser light; 1:31 “and, behold, it was very good,” JPS 1917)

Babylonian Talmud, Chagigah 12a (the light created on the first day; by it the first human saw from one end of the world to the other; God saw the generations of the Flood and of the Dispersion and hid it for the righteous in the time to come; Psalms 97:11)
Hasidic teaching that the hidden light was treasured in the Torah (Degel Machaneh Ephraim, Bereshit, in the name of the Baal Shem Tov)
